553: And the custom is, etc. - For Torah gladdens the heart; nevertheless, all of this is not required by strict law, since by law one is permitted to study all the matters that are permitted to be studied on Tisha B'Av itself even on its eve, and the main reason [for the restriction beforehand] is that one is [otherwise] able to study the things permitted [to be studied] on Tisha B'Av [and so should save them for then]. Now, it appears that many later authorities (Acharonim) accepted this custom and did not challenge it. Indeed, even if it falls on Shabbos, several Acharonim agreed to conduct themselves as the Rema wrote, as I will write further on. However, there are some Acharonim who raised serious objections to this custom. First among them is the Rashal, who wrote of himself that he studied [these forbidden topics] after midday and permitted this for others as well; also the Gra in his commentary wrote that this is an excessive stringency; and likewise the Ma'amar Mordechai elaborates at length on this in his work, writing that it leads many people to neglect of Torah study, since those who study come to be lax about studying the things that are permitted on Tisha B'Av, for a person only studies what his heart desires and therefore his opinion is to be lenient in this, and he writes that this is how he himself conducted himself, see there. And likewise the Chayei Adam wrote that this is merely a stringency. Therefore it appears that one who wishes to be lenient in this matter is not to be protested against.
